capabilities: Create question/answer and cloze cards from selected text
Run timed review sessions of 2, 5, 10 or custom minutes
Grade cards with FSRS scheduling and a desired retention setting
Group cards into folder-based decks and subdecks
Merge review state from several devices through file sync
disambiguation: Not a note-resurfacing or "on this day" tool; it schedules flashcards made from your notes.
extras: Manual install from release files until it reaches the community plugin list; no importer from other flashcard plugins and it does not read their scheduling data; no network requests or telemetry; editing the same deck file on two devices before syncing can create a sync conflict.
intentEvidence: These are good plugins; they solve different problems.
motivation: Built for people who want to remember what they read and write in their vault and who have tried flashcards before and watched the pile of due cards grow until they stopped.
problem: Flashcard plugins that pile up overdue cards, require inline syntax inside notes, or depend on Anki make a daily review habit hard to keep.

relations.evidence: If you like writing Question::Answer next to your prose, or want whole-note review, Spaced Repetition is built for that.
If you already live in Anki, or want its mobile apps, add-ons and sync, use Obsidian_to_Anki or Flashcards.

summary: Spaced repetition flashcard plugin using FSRS that runs timed review sessions of 2, 5 or 10 minutes, with cards kept as plain Markdown in their own folder.
